newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - FX vols cool as dollar firms back up.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FX vols cool as dollar firms back up.

text.p: Implied volatility levels for dollar-pair options softened in U.S. trading Tuesday as the spot dollar bounced back above 1.7100 marks and 126.00 yen.
After Monday's dip, dollar/mark rebounded in European trading on an outlook from Germany's six leading economic institutes for the dollar to average 1.80 marks in 1998.
One-month dollar/mark volatility slipped about 0.15 point from Monday, to 8.50/8.80 percent. One-year declined to 9.00/9.10 percent from 9.05/9.25 percent previously.
Options analysts said bearish sentiment toward the dollar, so evident Monday, appeared to wane as dollar-call/mark-put buyers re-entered the market and risk reversals narrowed.
Risk reversals, the put/call pricing differential, were marginally favoring mark calls at flat to 0.2 on one-month 25-delta options, but had pulled in from Monday's wider skew.

An options desk manager for a U.S. brokerage firm said the dollar most likely would continue to range-trade until this weekend's Group of Seven meeting is past. Longer term, he said, he looks for economic fundamentals to push dollar/mark to a test of 1.7500 in the next three months.

Traders observed the risk reversal spread for mark/franc options was retaining its strong mark call bias after the skew increased sharply following Monday's call for snap parliamentary elections in France.

Mark/franc volatility, traditionally low, climbed to 1.50/1.80 percent, from 0.80/1.00 percent, for one-month options after French President Jacques Chirac announced his decision to hold elections on May 25 and June 1.
In dollar/yen, risk reversals have resumed a dollar call bias, reversing the yen call slant that developed Monday when the dollar was edging toward 125.00 yen.
One-month 25-delta risk reversals were at 0.1 to 0.3 in favor of dollar calls.
Dollar/yen volatilities also weakened slightly, to 8.80/9.00 percent for one-month options and 9.85/10.00 percent for one-year dates.

A New York-based trader for a Japanese bank said market participants holding long gamma positions in dollar/yen were content to see the spot trade in a choppy fashion. The trader said a large dollar/yen strangle with strike parameters at about 124.50 and 127.30 had supplied the market with a "huge" gamma position.

"Many people got long gamma on the back of that big options play," he said. The large position is widely expected to expire Friday, in time for the meeting of G-7 finance ministers and central bankers.

Market participants would then be expected to buy volatility on Thursday and Friday, bracing for any remarks that could pry the dollar from its range. The trader predicted dollar/yen would return to a 120.00-125.00 range if the G-7 produces steps for stabilizing the foreign exchange market.
